hourly.summary: United fans are in full-blown crisis mode: managerial merry-go-round chaos (Wilcox vs Bloom, Allegri as 'cheap disaster', Deschamps issuing demands, Nagelsmann's skateboard mocked), a striker crisis so bad even the U18s can't finish, a defence needing a full backline rebuild, zero Champions League money, and fan protests ending in arrests. The gallows humour is peak — 'cheaper to buy Brighton' sums up the 'we're screwed for a long time' mood perfectly.

daily.summary: Fan sentiment remains stuck in a frustrated, resigned rut across the day, averaging a low 4/10 as injury woes, managerial confusion, and Glazer anger compound the post-Ferguson identity crisis. While morning discussions churn through managerial candidates and transfer targets with active frustration, the mood deepens into gallows humour and resignation by evening, with even a win dismissed as merely keeping United above Coventry. A stubborn thread of faith in academy graduates provides the only consistent counter-narrative to the prevailing gloom.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a cataclysmic 2/10 crisis throughout the week, briefly punctuated only by a fleeting false dawn on October 28th when Kobbie Mainoo's return temporarily lifted spirits to 7/10 before injury setbacks and dressing-room fractures crashed the mood back to rock bottom. The dominant arc is one of deepening structural resignation: a nine-game winless streak, genuine relegation fears, unified fury at the Glazers and INEOS, and a pervasive belief that the squad has downed tools have calcified the fanbase into radioactive gallows humor and total abandonment of hope.
